title: French GCSE revision
subtitle: AQA 8652, Year 10: free time, identity and relationships

conversation: Answer in the tense of the question
Give a detail: when, where, who with, how often
Give an opinion with a reason (parce que...)
Add a different time frame: past (j'ai...) or future (je vais... / je voudrais...)
roleplay: Cover every prompt, one clear sentence each
Keep it simple and accurate rather than long
Use the tense the prompt needs
For the question prompt, use a question word or est-ce que
read-aloud: Do not pronounce most final consonants or the -ent of verbs
Watch nasal sounds (an, en, on, in) and é / è
Answer the follow-up questions in full sentences, in the right tense
dictation: Listen once for meaning, then write sentence by sentence
Check verb endings and agreements make sense
Add accents: é, è, à, ç
Re-read what you wrote against what you hear
photo: Use il y a and the present tense
Say who, where and what they are doing
Keep each sentence short and accurate
grammar: Look at the subject: who is doing it?
Check gender and number for adjectives
Check the tense from the time phrase
After a negative, un / du / des become de
translate-fr: Translate the meaning, not word for word
Spot the tense of each sentence first
Do not leave gaps: use a simpler word if stuck
translate-en: Translate every word, including small ones (souvent, très, aussi)
Get the tense right in English (j'ai vu = I saw)
Make it sound like natural English
write-short: One or two sentences per bullet point
Present tense is fine at this level
write-90: Cover all three bullet points equally
Use past, present and future across the answer
Add connectives and one complex structure
write-150: Cover both bullet points in detail
Show a range of tenses: perfect, imperfect, future, conditional
Justify opinions and add complex structures (qui, ce qui, si...)
Leave time to check verbs and agreements

about:
French revision for a Year 10 assessment, built from the class topic list for Unit 1 (Free time) and Unit 2 (Identity and relationships), and set out to match the AQA GCSE French specification (8652, first exams 2026). Model answers, questions and translations were written for revision; they are not real past-paper questions.

The speaker buttons use your device's built-in French voice, so they work offline on most phones. If you hear English, install a French voice in your phone's settings.

Always check anything you are unsure about with your teacher. The official specification is at aqa.org.uk.
